quotes.quote: Husky users get copy-paste instructions for durable integration; other managers get a note to re-run `entire enable` if hooks are overwritten.

fence.reason: verdict is decision; Fence only changes code on a mistake verdict and asked a human instead
fence.question: runs/questions/2263.md

compare.what: Per issue and mode: fence = investigate, then fix only on a mistake verdict; baseline = the issue goes straight to the same worker. Both are verified the same way (the worker's test must fail without its fix, pass with it, nothing regresses).
limits: Each cell is one run; worker output and cost vary between runs.
Baseline cost has no investigation in it; fence cost includes the verdict call.
"verified" says the worker's own test passes and nothing in the tested packages regressed. It does not say the change is the fix a maintainer would want.

eval.what: Fence verdict (investigate only, at the issue-creation commit, no search fallback, no memory) for every closed issue that locates by name and traces to at least one checkpoint, compared with the issue's state_reason.
limits: A classifier that always answered "mistake" would agree on 45 of 47 of these issues; Fence agrees on 40 of 47. This comparison does not show that the verdict adds information; it mostly shows that the set is dominated by completed issues.
state_reason is a weak label. "completed" also covers feature work and refactors that were done as asked, where "mistake" (nobody chose the old behaviour) is not really the question being answered.
The not_planned set that locates by name and traces to a checkpoint is very small, so the decision side of this comparison is a handful of issues and its rate means little.
not_planned is not the same as a deliberate decision: issues are also closed that way as duplicates, as folded into another issue, or for process reasons.
Only issues that name a Go file or symbol and trace to at least one public checkpoint are included; that is a minority of closed issues, and probably the better-specified ones.
Each issue was run once. The verdict varies between runs of the same issue, so single cells can flip.
no_record is an abstention (Fence would ask a human) and is counted separately, not as agreement or disagreement.

decisions.title: Checkpoint data not pushed when agent commits and pushes in the same turn
decisions.quote: Add TurnEndHandler optional interface and implement it on ManualCommitStrategy to dispatch deferred condensation at turn end.
decisions.did: confirmed it as a real problem (khaong, 2026-02-12), a contributor PR (#303) was closed unmerged, and on 2026-04-28 ashtom labelled it `wontfix`: they "don't have a universal solution". The issue's state_reason is `completed`, but nothing was fixed.
decisions.note: Deferring condensation to turn end is a recorded design choice and the reported symptom follows directly from it. Maintainers kept the design. `decision` was the useful answer here; the `completed` label that counts this row as a disagreement in the eval is wrong about what happened.

decisions.title: Refactor hasTTY() to use optional agent interface
decisions.quote: Like Gemini CLI, the subprocess may inherit the user's TTY but can't respond to interactive prompts.
decisions.did: declined the proposed agent interface (PR #658 closed unmerged). Soph closed it 2026-06-01 as "Resolved by centralization rather than the agent-interface approach proposed here": the same hardcoded environment checks were moved into an `interactive` package.
decisions.note: Each hardcoded check was added on purpose and they are still hardcoded. This is a refactor request, so mistake-or-decision is a poor fit, but Fence's reading that the current shape was chosen matches the maintainers keeping it.

decisions.title: Cursor inadvertently invokes Claude Code hooks when `.cursor/hooks.json` is not installed
decisions.quote: SessionStart hint: first agent to fire claims the session ID
decisions.did: fixed it. PR #1263, merged 2026-06-25, added a guard that skips a hook forwarded from another agent's session; the first-writer-wins model was left in place.
decisions.note: First-writer-wins was chosen to settle a race when both hook files exist. Nobody chose misattribution when Cursor's hook file is absent, and Fence's rationale says so itself ("the gap when Cursor hooks are absent was not addressed"). This should have been `mistake`.

decisions.note: The quotes show the deprecation was deliberate, which the issue takes as given. The issue asks for the planned follow-up. Nothing here is a decision someone would be overriding. Confidence was 0.60, the lowest of the six.

decisions.title: entire status collapses multiple sessions per agent, and mutates session state while repo…
decisions.quote: **status finalizes too** — reverted to your original 'finalize on detection' intent now that status isn't a hot path.

decisions.title: Hook latency: remaining work after #2002
decisions.quote: writeCompactTranscript now uses compact.FullWithBoundary to write the entire compacted session into transcript.jsonl on every checkpoint

Its latency cost is what the issue reports, and Fence's rationale says "the latency cost was not weighed in the record". A tracking issue for performance work, already being done. Confidence 0.62.

decisions.title: Lefthook is classified as not overwriting Entire's hooks
decisions.quote: Husky users get copy-paste instructions for durable integration; other managers get a note to re-run `entire enable` if hooks are overwritten.
decisions.did: nothing merged. PR #2331 (fix Lefthook overwrite detection) is open; PR #2365 was closed unmerged.
decisions.reading: real choice, open, possibly on a wrong premise
decisions.note: Treating Lefthook as non-overwriting was explicit in the original commit. The issue argues the premise was factually wrong. That is a decision for a human to revisit, which is what `decision` asks for. See `runs/compare.json` for what the baseline worker did with this issue unasked.

decisions.title: ULID checkpoint refs unreadable when their shard case-collides on a case-insensitive file…
decisions.quote: Collapse it to a single positional rule: the last two characters, for both legacy 12-hex IDs and 26-char ULIDs.
decisions.did: PR #2406 (compare the shard case-insensitively) was closed unmerged. No maintainer comment on the issue.
decisions.note: The shard rule and the strict parse were chosen for determinism. Case-insensitive filesystems appear nowhere in the record, as Fence's rationale admits. The closed PR hints the maintainers want a different fix, but that is a guess; nothing recorded says the data loss was accepted.

decisions.title: Commit linking attaches an unrelated Codex session from another worktree
decisions.quote: nearest ancestor wins, ties go to the most recently interacting session, start times guard against PID reuse
decisions.did: agreed it is a bug. Soph, 2026-09-28: "The diagnosis checks out." PRs #2531 and #2621 are open; #2621 is titled "break shared-owner ties by environment and phase, not recency".
decisions.note: The tie-break rule was chosen before Codex moved every session into one daemon process, which makes every tie resolve wrongly. Fence's rationale: "the concurrent shared-daemon case wasn't considered". Should have been `mistake`; the maintainer treats it as one. Confidence 0.60.
